The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
Why, in plain words: A pricing service the shop asks for each shopper's basket total began answering slowly, and the shop's account pages likely waited for it with no time limit, even though they can be shown without that total.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 9m 0s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: restarted io-pricing - confirmed
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #523 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
Incident: HighLatency on io-shop
Date: Nov 10, 2026, 23:12 to 23:21 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 10, 2026, 23:28:44 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 10, 2026, 23:19:27 UTC
Ended by: Argus: restarted io-pricing - confirmed, nothing to put back

Summary
The service broke at 23:12 UTC and was back to normal at 23:21 UTC, 9 minutes later. What its alert watches went from 215 ms before it began to 1722 ms at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A pricing service the shop asks for each shopper's basket total began answering slowly, and the shop's account pages likely waited for it with no time limit, even though they can be shown without that total. What Argus did: restarted io-pricing - confirmed, nothing to put back. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #523, for a person to review and merge. If io-pricing slows down again, every account page could again slow down by the same amount.

Impact
9m 0s - onset until back to normal
1.0% to 0.6% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
215 ms to 1434 ms - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 1722 ms; the rule's line is 600 ms)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
basket_total, which _the_basket_for calls to fetch the account page's optional basket total, sets no limit on how long it waits for io-pricing, so when io-pricing's basket-total calls began taking 1500ms, every account page waited out the whole call. The page's existing fallback, which renders it without the total, only runs on PricingServiceFailed, and a slow answer never raises that. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The latency of io-shop's slowest requests rose past the alert's line and stayed there until the alert fired.
  Evidence:
    AL1 p95 latency above threshold for 5m
why 1 From the onset, io-shop's calls to io-pricing for each shopper's basket total took 1500ms each, logged as slow upstream calls over 23:12–23:19 UTC. The slowness came from io-pricing, the internal service owned by checkout-platform.
  Evidence:
    G9feb WARN io-shop: slow upstream call - pricing.io-internal.svc took 1500ms for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 23:12–23:19; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total took 8 different values; # was 43 to 200, typically 200, highest at 23:13
    T5 23:19:55 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 23:12
    T20 23:23:09 Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - restarted io-pricing and the rule that fired stopped firing
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 10 23:13; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes.
      T7
      T8
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 23:19:59.
      T14
why 2 Each account page waited for that call to finish. _the_basket_for calls basket_total on the page's path, and basket_total sets no limit on how long it waits, so a slow answer was waited out in full instead of failing over to the page's existing fallback without the total.
  Evidence:
    U1 basket_total at src/io_shop/account_page.py:183, in _the_basket_for: calls it: return basket_total(shopper_id, ask_the_pricing_service), None
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No review or test check was seen that requires calls from io-shop to its dependencies to have a time limit. Code-Fix's reading says io-shop's existing tests expected a slow pricing answer to come back as a price. (AI-3)
- io-pricing's slowdown was found only by io-shop's latency alert. No alert on io-pricing's own latency was seen, and nothing was seen alerting on the slow-upstream-call warnings io-shop logged from the onset. (AI-4, AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | io-pricing, an internal service owned by checkout-platform, began taking about 1500ms per basket-total call at 23:12. The account page waits on it, so p50, p95 and p99 all jumped. io-shop itself is healthy: nothing was deployed or changed, and CPU, memory and error rate are flat. | 0.90 | confirmed

Trigger
C1 was confirmed; it blames io-pricing, whose deploys Argus did not read.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 23:20:04 | Restarted io-pricing for C1 | Argus | nothing to put back | confirmed
 | 23:25:15 | Proposed a fix: PR #523 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 23:12 UTC. HighLatency fired at 23:19:05 UTC, 7 minutes 5 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | p95 latency above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Restarted io-pricing | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #523 | open
AI-3 | Add a review or lint check requiring every outbound call from io-shop to a dependency to set a time limit. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a latency alert on io-pricing's basket-total endpoint, owned by checkout-platform. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add an alert on the rate of io-shop's slow-upstream-call warnings for each dependency. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Have checkout-platform find out why io-pricing's basket-total calls slowed down and what restarting it cleared. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route io-shop's HighLatency alert to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes 5 seconds after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 54 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 54 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 23:19:59.
- 59 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent restarted io-pricing, a dependency of io-shop for C1.
- 4 minutes 4 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 6 minutes 10 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #523.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 10 23:12 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began

T8 | 23:19:57 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 production changes

T16 | 23:20:04 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Restarted io-pricing, a dependency of io-shop for C1
T17 | 23:20:12 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 23:21 - up to 234s

T18 | 23:23:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 23:20
T19 | 23:23:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T20 | 23:23:09 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - restarted io-pricing and the rule that fired stopped firing

Response effort
none - engineer time
211,373 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/5ea48632-20fd-4411-931d-37a802cf20a2
The fix it proposed: PR #523 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/523) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 57 occurrences in 38 minutes, 22:42–23:19
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 35 occurrences in 38 minutes, 22:42–23:19; # was 0.50% to 3.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 22:50
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 3 occurrences in 18 minutes, 22:59–23:16
G9feb | WARN io-shop: slow upstream call - pricing.io-internal.svc took 1500ms for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 23:12–23:19; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total took 8 different values; # was 43 to 200, typically 200, highest at 23:13
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: the basket total is optional. The account page already shows without it when pricing gives no price, because _the_basket_for catches PricingServiceFailed. But basket_total set no limit on how long it would wait for an answer. When io-pricing started taking 1500ms, every account page waited the full 1500ms, and io-shop's p50 went from 45ms to about 1546ms. io-shop did no retrying, fell back on nothing and never gave up. It just wrote a log line about how slow the call was and kept waiting. So someone else's slowdown became io-shop's latency in full, for something the page can do without.

The fix, all in pricing_service.basket_total:
• A new limit, PRICING_BUDGET_MS = 300. The normal call is around 12ms, and the existing warning threshold is 200ms.
• The call now runs on a small worker pool, and the code waits for it with future.result(timeout=...). A call that hangs or crawls is given up on after the limit, whatever the network does.
• If the service reports that the call took longer than the limit, that also counts as running out of time. The service is reached through a function the caller passes in, and that function reports how long the call took.
• Either way, PricingServiceFailed is raised with a message naming the host, the path and the limit. The account page already catches that and renders the page with "Pricing is not available right now", keeping the message as pricing_failure.

Nothing is hidden: errors other than running out of time still pass through unchanged, a no-price answer still fails the same way, and calls between 200ms and 300ms still return a price and are still reported as slow. account_page.py doesn't need to change because it already treats PricingServiceFailed as "show the page without the basket".

Tests:
• A service that answers in 1500ms now leaves the page without its basket total. The old code returned the price, so this test fails against it.
• A service that blocks for real is given up on well within a second. The old code waited the whole time, so this test fails against it too.
• Calls that are slow but within the limit still return a price and a slow-call line.
• The two tests that expected a 1500ms answer to come back as a price now describe the new behaviour instead.
How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main
U1 | basket_total at src/io_shop/account_page.py:183, in _the_basket_for: calls it: return basket_total(shopper_id, ask_the_pricing_service), None
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop found that their account pages loaded slowly. The shop asks a pricing service for each shopper's basket total, and that service began answering slowly. The account pages likely waited for it with no time limit, even though they can be shown without that total. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. No one on call was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus restarted the pricing service, and that restart has been confirmed. Argus has also proposed a lasting fix. It is still an unreviewed draft, so it has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
